description: HAL I2C1 + AT24C02 EEPROM (0x50): 16 bytes written across two page boundaries with ACK polling, read back blocking (N = 16/1/2) and with interrupts, 'eeprom ok' on USART1
expect:
72 MHz. I2C1 PB6/PB7 AF open-drain, 100 kHz, event+error interrupts; AT24C02 at 0x50 (A2-A0 and WP at GND) with 4.7 kOhm pull-ups; USART1 PA9/PA10 115200 8N1. Once after reset: 'AT24C02 test
'; no ACK from 0x50 (IsDeviceReady, 3 trials) -> 'eeprom not found at 0x50
' and stop. Else 'before: ' + the 16 bytes at 0x1C as hex (FF on an erased part; A0..AF after an earlier run: the EEPROM is non-volatile) + '
'; then A0+i is written to 0x1C+i in page-aligned pieces, each followed by ACK polling through the 5 ms write cycle: 'wrote 4 bytes at 0x1C, ready after P polls
', 'wrote 8 bytes at 0x20, ...', 'wrote 4 bytes at 0x28, ...' (P about 45: one NACKed poll takes about 112 us); then 'read 16 ok
' (Mem_Read 16 bytes), 'read 1 ok
' (1 byte at 0x1C), 'read 2 ok
' (2 bytes at 0x1D, POS procedure), 'read 16 (IT) ok
' (Mem_Read_IT) and 'eeprom ok
'; then WFI. A wrong byte prints 'mismatch at 0xAA: wrote 0xWW read 0xRR (<mode>)
', a HAL failure '<step> error: HAL status S, ErrorCode 0xE
', and the program stops there.

circuit: PB6, PB7: AT24C02 (A2-A0, WP to GND) + 4.7k pull-ups to 3V3
USART1: virtual terminal on PA9 (TX) / PA10 (RX)

USART1.match:
^AT24C02 test
before: (?:(?:FF ){15}FF|A0 A1 A2 A3 A4 A5 A6 A7 A8 A9 AA AB AC AD AE AF)
wrote 4 bytes at 0x1C, ready after (?:3[5-9]|4[0-9]|50) polls
wrote 8 bytes at 0x20, ready after (?:3[5-9]|4[0-9]|50) polls
wrote 4 bytes at 0x28, ready after (?:3[5-9]|4[0-9]|50) polls
read 16 ok
read 1 ok
read 2 ok
read 16 \(IT\) ok
eeprom ok
$
